# JOURNAL — building azion.com + Azion Docs with WebKit 5.12.0 (eval-m27 / B)

Builder: Claude (Opus 5.5), acting as an Azion web developer new to WebKit. All times UTC, 2026-11-12.
Only sources used: `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit` (README, llms/, skills/, rules/, adapters/, catalog.json, blocks/, examples/) and `npx @aziontech/webkit …`. Reference designs: `eval-m27/ref/pages.json` + `ref/shots/`.

## 05:26 — Setup (≈2 min wall clock; timestamps in this journal come from `date` on the machine)

- Read `ref/README.md` + `pages.json` descriptions for the 8 site/docs pages. Tiled the tall reference PNGs with `ref/tools/tile.sh` so I could look at them.
- `npm install` of vue/vue-router/vee-validate, then the three tarballs, then vite 6 + plugin-vue + tailwind v4 + vue-tsc.
- **Friction #1 — theme version mismatch.** `@aziontech/webkit@5.12.0` declares `"@aziontech/theme": "^4.0.0"`, but the theme I was given is 5.2.2. npm therefore pulled **theme 4.3.1 from the public registry** and nested it under `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/node_modules/`. Two theme copies in one app, and nothing told me. (Checked with `npm ls @aziontech/theme`.)
- npm 11 gates install scripts (`esbuild postinstall` not run) — esbuild still worked via its optional native package. Not WebKit's fault.
- Read the package README "For AI agents: start here". Clear and well-ordered: init → search → view → add → check. But it points at a **docs site (`apps/docs`, `pnpm docs:dev`) and demos that do not ship in the package**; for a consumer they don't exist. Several block descriptions also say "see Templates › Headers › SiteHeader" / "Templates › Marketing › Shell › SiteNav" — those are docs-site page names, not something I can open.
- `npx @aziontech/webkit init --dry-run` then `init -y`. Good: it kept my `file:` tarball deps (it plans `add-dep @aziontech/webkit@latest` in the dry run, which scared me, but didn't overwrite). It wrote `src/webkit.css`, `eslint.config.mjs`, `.stylelintrc.json`, `.mcp.json`, husky hook, `.claude/` rules+skills+agents, `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, and merged the two imports into `src/main.ts`.
- **Friction #2 — init assumes PostCSS.** It added `@tailwindcss/postcss` + `postcss.config.mjs` although `@tailwindcss/vite` was already in devDependencies. Running both would double-process Tailwind. I removed `postcss.config.mjs` and kept the Vite plugin.
- `init` also adds every dev dep as `"latest"` (eslint, stylelint, husky…) — unpinned ranges in package.json.
- AGENTS.md block is genuinely useful: flat imports, tokens only, "never restyle a webkit component", layout classes, `data-theme="dark"`.

## 05:28 — Discovery: is there a website and a docs starter?

- `npx @aziontech/webkit search marketing website home page` → `shells/website`, `headers/site-header`. `search documentation docs page sidebar` → `shells/documentation`, `headers/docs-header`, and the `Doc*` components. Search worked well on the first try.
- `view shells/website` / `view shells/documentation`: guidelines + the full SFC. Very good material.
- **Friction #3 — the shells don't use WebKit's own higher-level pieces.** `shells/website` hand-composes `GlobalHeader + NavigationMenu + Button…` and `Footer kind="site"`, while the catalog also ships `SiteNav` ("the marketing site's own navigation… plus the sheet below xl") and `SiteFooter`. `shells/documentation` hand-writes the "On this page" `<ul>` even though `DocOnThisPage` exists, and has no `DocPageHeader`/`DocProse`. Which one is canonical? Nothing says.
- Both shells contain a hand-rolled `lgProbe` (appends a `<span class="hidden lg:block">` to body, reads computed style on resize) just to move the brand mark in the footer. That is a lot of boilerplate to copy into every app; the Footer should own it.
- `llms/llms.txt` index is the best map: sections "Components: Marketing", "Components: Marketing sections" (≈55 page sections named after real azion.com bands: HeroBand, PlatformDirectory, NetworkSection, RecognitionMarquee, ClientMosaic, PricingPlans, ComparePlans, FaqSection, CodeSplit, QuoteTabs, HeroForm, ContactHub, ClosingCallToAction…) and "Components: Documentation" (DocPageHeader, DocCallout, DocSteps, DocCodeGroup, DocTabs, DocCard(Group), DocItem, DocOnThisPage, DocPagination, DocPrompt, DocFrame, DocCta…). On paper almost every band in the 8 designs has a named component.

## 05:30 — Decisions for the app

- **One app** (Vite 6 + Vue 3.5 + TS + Vue Router) serving `/`, `/pricing`, `/products/functions`, `/contact` and `/documentation/**`, prerendered with **vite-ssg** (static HTML per route for SEO). WebKit rendered under SSR without a single complaint — good sign (`webkit-provider`, sections, marquees, maps all SSR'd).
- Site chrome: chose the **`SiteNav` + `SiteFooter` sections** over copying `shells/website` (the shell hand-builds what those sections already are). Layout = sticky `SiteNav`, `HeroBand` per page, then `SectionContainer max-width="site"` with `SectionGap hatch` between sections, `SiteFooter kind="site"` — exactly the `webkit-sections` rule.
- Dark-only site: `useHead({ htmlAttrs: { 'data-theme': 'dark' } })` in the site layout (AGENTS.md: "for dark set `<html data-theme="dark">`").
- vite-ssg quirk (not WebKit): child routes of `/` must be absolute (`/pricing`) or nested ones (`products/functions`) prerender empty. Cost me a few minutes of reading vite-ssg source.

## 05:30–05:38 — Site pages (wall clock ≈8 min of building for all four; Home took the longest because the asset/registry hunt happened there)

Process per page: read `pages.json` description → map each band to a section in `llms.txt` "Marketing sections" → read `llms/components/<name>.md` (Props table + first example) → write the page as data. Almost no markup of my own.

| Reference band                                              | WebKit section used                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hero + logo strip                                           | `HeroBand kind="centered"` with `highlight`/`title` + `carouselMarks` (Home); `kind="title-band"` (Pricing, Functions — framework marks in the same floor)          |
| Primitives grid (4 cols)                                    | `PlatformDirectory`                                                                                                                                                 |
| Network band + client outcomes                              | `NetworkSection kind="outcomes"`                                                                                                                                    |
| Why Azion 4 cells                                           | `FeatureTiles kind="artwork"`                                                                                                                                       |
| 5 use-case rows                                             | `MediaSplitStack` (alternating on Functions)                                                                                                                        |
| Recognition carousel                                        | `RecognitionMarquee`                                                                                                                                                |
| Client stories mosaic                                       | `ClientMosaic`                                                                                                                                                      |
| Closing CTA                                                 | `ClosingCallToAction kind="primary"` / `kind="split"` (Functions "Build once. Run everywhere.")                                                                     |
| Plan cards + Monthly/Annual                                 | `PricingPlans`                                                                                                                                                      |
| Value props (3 illustrated)                                 | `FeatureTiles kind="illustrated"` with registry illustrations `no-idle-no-waste`, `stay-in-control`, `white-gloves-when-it-matters` (exact art from the live site!) |
| Feature comparison table, sticky header, mobile plan picker | `ComparePlans`                                                                                                                                                      |
| FAQ                                                         | `FaqSection`                                                                                                                                                        |
| Code showcase with sql/kv/storage/ai tabs                   | `CodeSplit`                                                                                                                                                         |
| Testimonial + logo tab row                                  | `ClientQuotes` (framed `QuoteTabs`)                                                                                                                                 |
| Contact hero + lead form                                    | `HeroForm` (fields as data, `submit` event, `loading/submitted/error` props)                                                                                        |
| Support 2×2 grid                                            | `ContactHub` (lanes + channels)                                                                                                                                     |

Result: all four site pages look like azion.com at 1440 on the first build. This is the strongest part of WebKit: the marketing sections are literally the azion.com bands, and the art (illustrations, client logos, analyst logos, photos) ships with the package.

Frictions found while doing it:

- **Friction #4 — example asset URLs don't resolve for a consumer.** Every marketing example uses `'/marketing-components/logos/dafiti-extended-mono.svg'`, `'/marketing-components/photos/netshoes.jpg'`… Those paths exist only in WebKit's docs app. The real way is `import logo from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/dafiti-extended-mono.svg'` (360 `./assets/*` exports in package.json). I found it by grepping `package.json` and `src/assets/site-assets.json` (a map from the example URL to the import). Only `quote-tabs`/`logo-wall`/`quote` examples show the import form. The examples should all use the import.
- **Friction #5 — registry names are undiscoverable.** `HeroBand.carouselMarks`, `Ticker.marks`, `ClientQuotes.items[].mark`, `FeatureTiles.tiles[].illustration`, `MediaSplitStack.bands[].illustration` take "registry names", but no doc lists them. I listed `src/assets/illustrations/registry.ts` and `src/assets/logos/*` by hand. Worse, some art is an _asset_ but not a _registry_ entry (`branches`, `personal-tokens`, `azion-highlight`, `usage-chart` must go through `image:` + import, the others through `illustration:`), so you need to know which is which. An unknown mark silently renders as a typographic wordmark — fine at runtime, but no warning.
- `FaqSection` example contains a broken rewritten link: `https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.specs/en/documentation/products/...` (the doc build rewrote a relative azion.com link into a GitHub `.specs` URL). The same rewriting makes every component page's "API as JSON" link point to `github.com/…/.specs/<name>.json`, which a consumer can't open — the local `llms/components/<name>.json` is the real one.
- Small layout deviations I accepted rather than fight (the rule says never restyle a section): Contact's support grid is 2 lanes + a 3-column channel row with one empty cell (reference: 2×2); HeroBand `title-length` changes the line breaking and the default matched better.

## 05:38–05:50 — Docs shell (≈5 min) and the four docs pages (≈7 min)

Discovery: `search documentation docs page sidebar` → `shells/documentation`, `headers/docs-header` and the `Doc*` family. I used the shell's frame (GlobalHeader + `Sidebar` with `ThemeSwitcher` in its footer + `Menu` + `ScrollArea` + footer inside the scroller) but replaced its hand-written outline with **`DocOnThisPage`** (+ `groups` for GitHub/Community) and **`DocCta`** ("Ready to build?"), and its hand-written `Footer` composition with **`SiteFooter kind="content"`**.

| Reference element                                                                        | WebKit piece                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Header with DOCS tag, section tabs, GitHub, Console                                      | `GlobalHeader` + `NavigationMenu` + `IconButton` + `Button` (copied from the block)                                 |
| Left rail, collapsible groups, active pill, theme switch, « collapse                     | `Sidebar collapsible` + data-driven `Menu` (`groups`, `active-id`, inline subs, `navigate` event) + `ThemeSwitcher` |
| Mobile: hamburger → nav sheet                                                            | `Drawer` + `DrawerPortal/Overlay/Content` + `PanelHeader/PanelContent` + the same `Menu`                            |
| Breadcrumb, H1, lead, "Last updated · Copy as Markdown · View as Markdown · Agent setup" | `DocPageHeader` (`breadcrumb`, `lastUpdated`, `metaActions`) — exact match of the reference meta row                |
| Prose rhythm, inline code chips, links                                                   | `DocProse` (styles descendants; components opt out with `data-doc-chrome`)                                          |
| H2 with anchor                                                                           | `DocHeading` + `provideHeadingNav` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-heading-nav`) to scroll the inner scroller               |
| Info / tip callouts                                                                      | `DocCallout kind="info"                                                                                             | "tip"` |
| Numbered steps with connector                                                            | `DocSteps` / `DocStep`                                                                                              |
| Code blocks with language label, line numbers, copy                                      | `DocCodeGroup` (on `CodeBlock`)                                                                                     |
| Homebrew/Windows/RPM/dpkg/APK/APT tab strip                                              | `DocTabs` / `DocTab`                                                                                                |
| AI Assistant prompt card                                                                 | `DocPrompt`                                                                                                         |
| Link-card grids, chooser rows, Next steps                                                | `DocCardGroup` + `DocCard` (`link-label` gives the blue "Action ›" row)                                             |
| Related resources list with chevrons                                                     | `FrameBox` + `ItemList` + `DocItem`                                                                                 |
| Request-path / CLI flow diagrams with copy button                                        | `DocFrame` + `Diagram name="applications"` (from the shipped library) / `Diagram :spec` (CLI)                       |
| Prev / next pager                                                                        | `DocPagination`                                                                                                     |
| "Your AI agent, fluent in Azion" 70/30 banner                                            | `Banner` (marketing)                                                                                                |
| ON THIS PAGE + GitHub/Community + promo                                                  | `DocOnThisPage` + `DocCta`                                                                                          |

Frictions in the docs part:

- **Friction #6 — no scroll-spy.** `DocOnThisPage` is "presentation only: `activeId` is a prop, because the page owns the scroll container". Every docs site needs the same IntersectionObserver/scroll logic; I hand-wrote ~30 lines (find the scroller, compute the active heading, smooth-scroll with offset). WebKit even owns the scroll container (`ScrollArea`) and the heading registry (`DocHeading`) — it should ship `useDocOutline()`.
- **Friction #7 — `ThemeSwitcher` "applies no global side effect"** and there is no `useTheme`/`useColorMode`. I wrote `use-docs-theme.ts` (resolve `system` via `matchMedia`, persist, write `data-theme`). My first version wrote the attribute directly and was silently overwritten by `useHead` — the docs rendered light in "dark". Every app will write this composable.
- **Friction #8 — `DocProse` leaks into WebKit `Button`s.** A `Button` with `href` renders an `<a>`, and DocProse's `a` rules paint it blue + underlined ("Applications reference" in link-blue on a black button). DocCallout/DocCard opt out via `data-doc-chrome`; `Button` doesn't. Workaround: wrap button rows in `<div data-doc-chrome>` (documented only inside `doc-prose.md` "Mark a documentation component's root `data-doc-chrome`"). Same for `Banner`.
- **Friction #9 — the `shells/documentation` block doesn't contain its scroller.** It wraps `ScrollArea` in `<div class="flex flex-1">` without `min-h-0`, so the ScrollArea grows to the article height, the _window_ scrolls instead, and the `h-screen` canvas ends at the first viewport. In light mode you barely notice; **in dark mode everything below the fold sits on the white `<body>`** (white-on-white headings, invisible code chips). I first blamed fonts/capture; measuring the DOM showed `ScrollArea h=4455` inside `main h=844`. Fix: `min-h-0` on that wrapper, plus `body { background: var(--bg-canvas) }` (the theme does not paint `body`). Both belong in WebKit.
- **Friction #10 — `drawer.md` documents the wrong component.** Its "Examples" section shows `Menu` code, so I built the drawer without `DrawerPortal`/`DrawerOverlay` and the closed drawer's content rendered inline at the bottom of the mobile page. The correct anatomy is in `examples/drawer/Default.vue`.
- `menu.md` is an internal spec dump (Kumo comparisons, "Exports to add to package.json", testid conflicts, file tree) — 300 lines to find that `groups` is `{ label?, items: MenuNode[] }`. I read `MenuNode` from `src/components/navigation/menu/injection-key.ts`.
- `DocCallout` has no title prop (reference "Rolling out —" title is bold text inside). `Banner` only takes a description in the _aside_, so the reference's left-column paragraph had to go; its marketing padding is tall for a docs page. The docs header search _field_ with `CTRL K` isn't in the block (it says "the sample widens the search into a field", but the shipped SFC is an icon button) — I kept the icon button.
- Markdown rendering bugs in `llms/`: broken backticks (`- useHeadingNav\` — …`), `1 \ \| 2 \ \| 3` in DocHeading's prop table.
- `SiteFooter`'s doc says "Inside the product console or the docs → compose `footer` directly", yet it has `kind: 'content'` for exactly that. I used it in the docs; it works.

## 05:50–05:58 — Quality gates, fixes, screenshots

- `npx @aziontech/webkit check`: first run **14 errors**. 13 were `authoring-standards` "Comment in implementation code" — the rule that forbids comments inside WebKit's own source is applied to the **consumer app** (it even flagged the `/// <reference types="vite/client" />` triple-slash directive and `// WebKit ships .vue sources` explanation comments). I deleted every comment and moved the rationale into this journal. 1 was real and useful: `Menu` imported from the compound `@aziontech/webkit/menu` → `menu-root` for tree-shaking.
- Doctor warned about 8 deps pinned as `"latest"` — which `init` itself wrote. Pinned them.
- **Remaining warning (false positive): "no postcss config — Tailwind v4 may not run in the build"**. Tailwind runs through `@tailwindcss/vite`; doctor only knows PostCSS.
- `vue-tsc --noEmit`: my code is clean, but **7 errors remain inside WebKit's own `compare-plans.vue`** (`Cannot find name 'section'`) — because WebKit ships `.vue` source, `skipLibCheck` doesn't help and a consumer's type-check inherits WebKit's type errors. I kept `vue-tsc` out of `npm run build` for that reason (`npm run typecheck` separately).
- Types I had to fix: `HeroFormField`, `NetworkSectionOutcome`, `ComparePlansRow`, `DiagramSpec` — all importable as `import type { X } from '@aziontech/webkit/<name>'` (good), but no doc says so; I found them by grepping the `.vue` files.
- **`ComparePlansRow.group` is a `boolean`** ("renders the row as a group heading"); the llms page says `{ label, values, group?, … }` without the type, and I'd assumed it was the group _name_ — the table rendered without its sub-group header rows until I read the source.
- `init` writes `import '@aziontech/icons'` into `main.ts`, which `vue-tsc` rejects ("Cannot find module or type declarations for side-effect import") — needed `declare module '@aziontech/icons'`.
- SSG: needed `ssr: { noExternal: ['@aziontech/webkit'] }` in `vite.config.ts` once a component whose subpath points at an `index.ts` (GlobalHeader compound) was imported: Node tried to `import` a `.vue` file. Not documented anywhere in the package (no mention of SSR/SSG setup at all), although WebKit itself is SSR-safe.
- Theme fonts: every page logs `404 https://fonts.azion.com/rubik/Rubik-VariableFont_wght.ttf` (and the italic). The `@font-face` has a jsDelivr fallback so text renders, but every page view pays a failed request + console error.
- `npx @aziontech/webkit report` lints `dist/` (minified bundles) and counts them as violations (56, from WebKit's own compiled code); it should ignore build output.
- Screenshots: Playwright 1.62 in docker, static server inside the container, 1440×900 and 390×844 (isMobile). Docs captured light + dark (dark via `prefers-color-scheme` + the theme preference), site dark-only. For docs the capture un-clips the inner `ScrollArea` so the full article is in one PNG (the reference did the equivalent by growing the viewport).

## Hand-written pieces (and why)

| Piece                                                                                                                                        | Why WebKit didn't cover it                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/docs/use-docs-theme.ts` (≈35 lines)                                                                                                     | No theme/color-mode composable; ThemeSwitcher is side-effect free by design.                                                                                                                                               |
| Scroll-spy + scroll-to-heading in `DocsLayout.vue` (≈35 lines)                                                                               | `DocOnThisPage` is presentation-only; no outline composable.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `DocsLayout.vue` frame (header, rail, scroller, outline aside)                                                                               | Copied from `shells/documentation` (via `view`), swapped in `DocOnThisPage`, `DocCta`, `SiteFooter`, a `Drawer` for mobile, and fixed the `min-h-0`. A docs layout component (or a working shell) would remove ~150 lines. |
| `<div data-doc-chrome>` wrappers around button rows / Banner                                                                                 | DocProse styles `<a>` buttons.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Docs nav trees / outlines data (`nav.ts`)                                                                                                    | Content, not UI — expected.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Docs-home H1 + lead + "Copy prompt" row                                                                                                      | `DocPageHeader` is article-shaped (breadcrumb + meta). A docs landing hero (H1, lead, two actions, caption) doesn't exist in the Doc family; `HeroBand` is marketing-sized.                                                |
| `body { background: var(--bg-canvas) }` in `webkit.css`                                                                                      | The theme doesn't paint `body`.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Site: nothing but data files (`chrome.ts`, `pricing-data.ts`) and two layout wrappers (`sticky top-0`, footer border) copied from the shell. |

## What WebKit must change so this is effortless

1. **Fix the shells and make them use the family.** `shells/documentation`: `min-h-0` around `ScrollArea`, paint the canvas, use `DocOnThisPage`, `DocCta`, `DocPageHeader`, `SiteFooter kind="content"`, a mobile `Drawer` with the same `Menu`. `shells/website`: use `SiteNav` + `SiteFooter`. Better: ship `DocsLayout` / `SiteLayout` components so the frame isn't copied.
2. **Ship `useDocOutline()`** (scroll-spy + scroll-to-heading for the `ScrollArea`) and **`useColorMode()`** (system/dark/light → `data-theme`, persisted, SSR-safe).
3. **Examples must run as pasted in a consumer app.** Replace every `'/marketing-components/…'` URL with `import x from '@aziontech/webkit/assets/…'`; fix `drawer.md` (shows Menu's examples); fix the rewritten `.specs` links and the broken Markdown in `llms/`.
4. **Document registry names**: one list (or `npx @aziontech/webkit view marks|illustrations|diagrams`) of every `mark`, `illustration`, diagram and asset, and say which props take a registry name vs an imported URL. Warn in dev when a mark is unknown.
5. **Put types in the docs**: show `import type { HeroFormField } …` and expand inline types in prop tables (`group?: boolean`, not `group?`).
6. **Keep consumer type-checks green**: fix `compare-plans.vue`'s TS errors; ship a `@aziontech/icons` declaration; consider shipping `.d.ts` for SFCs.
7. **Document SSR/SSG**: `ssr.noExternal: ['@aziontech/webkit']` for Vite SSR / vite-ssg, and that everything renders server-side (it does — that's a selling point nobody is told).
8. **Tooling should understand Vite**: `init` shouldn't add `@tailwindcss/postcss` when `@tailwindcss/vite` is present; `doctor` shouldn't warn "no postcss config"; `init` shouldn't write `"latest"` and then have `doctor` complain about it; `report` must ignore `dist/`.
9. **Scope the authoring rules**: "no comments in implementation code" is a rule for WebKit's own source, not for apps; don't enable it in the consumer preset (and never flag `///` directives).
10. **DocProse must not style WebKit components**: `Button`, `Banner` and other WebKit roots should carry `data-doc-chrome` (or DocProse should exclude `[data-testid]` roots).
11. **Fix the dependency graph**: webkit 5.12 → `@aziontech/theme ^4` while the matching theme is 5.x, so a second theme is installed from npm; fix the Rubik 404 on fonts.azion.com.
12. Docs gaps for the docs surface: a docs landing hero, a `DocCallout` title, a search _field_ with ⌘K in the docs header block, `Banner` with a leading-column description.

## Summary

WebKit is remarkably complete for this job: every band of the four marketing designs and almost every docs element map to a named, data-driven component, the azion.com art (illustrations, client and analyst logos, photos) ships in the package, and everything server-renders under vite-ssg. The four marketing pages were nearly pure data and looked like azion.com on the first build. The friction is at the edges: documentation that doesn't run as pasted (asset URLs, a wrong example, untyped prop docs), two blocks that are worse than the components they sit next to (and one, the docs shell, that is broken in dark mode), missing app-level composables (theme, outline), and tooling tuned for WebKit's own repo rather than for a Vite consumer (PostCSS assumption, comment rule, `latest` pins, `report` scanning `dist/`, WebKit's own TS errors leaking into the app's type-check).

Final gate: `npx @aziontech/webkit check` → **0 errors, 1 warning** (the PostCSS false positive) — see `check.txt`. `npm run build` (vite-ssg) builds all 8 routes to static HTML. `vue-tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors in app code, 7 inside `node_modules/@aziontech/webkit/…/compare-plans.vue`.
